gen-luckiest-guy-gf-noto-sans-tirhuta: Loud, cheerful shapes that look like cable bent into letters. Luckiest Guy is best at shouting in one unvarying line, while Noto Sans Tirhuta is best at staying quiet, with cut-back terminals and a dominant x-height.
gen-luckiest-guy-gf-noto-sans-vai: Cheerful one-nib shouting from Luckiest Guy, with its mean line set high. Noto Sans Vai sits below with words that read as solid blocks, leaving generous space between curve ends and stems.
gen-luckiest-guy-gf-noto-sans-wancho: Ink that looks poured at a single width makes Luckiest Guy loud and cheerful, with a mean line set high. Paragraphs in Noto Sans Wancho read like thick chalk pressed hard.
gen-luckiest-guy-gf-noto-sans-warang-cit: Cheerful and loud, Luckiest Guy lays down a plain stripe of constant ink with its mean line set high. Noto Sans Warang Citi gives that noise somewhere to rest.
gen-luckiest-guy-gf-noto-sans-yi: Loud, cheerful and outlined in one steady thickness all round, Luckiest Guy hangs its mean line high. Noto Sans Yi keeps a deep midsection and rounds left unlatched.
gen-luckiest-guy-gf-oxygen: Curves that never close back on themselves keep the body open beneath Luckiest Guy, loud and cheerful. Oxygen can be nudged larger, since its lowercase nearly matches the capitals.
gen-luckiest-guy-gf-puritan: Poured-ink letters of Luckiest Guy shout cheerfully from a high mean line. What holds the pair together is Puritan, whose rounded sans-serif forms stay open to the side and whose e and a counters are oversized.
gen-flavors-gf-noto-sans-sundanese: Whimsical and commanding, Flavors stamps flat single-weight linework with a stubby, towering x-height. Noto Sans Sundanese does the quieter job, with open-mouthed e crossbars and caps barely taller than the lowercase.
gen-gf-oxanium-gf-sono: Sono arrives tall in the lowercase, with generous spacing between letters. What stands out most is a shared openness: Oxanium's curves end in clear daylight, and Sono leaves each a ajar.
gen-gf-paprika-gf-stack-sans-headline: Stack Sans Headline holds a monoline skeleton beneath Paprika, whose lowercase fills the line like capitals. Stack Sans Headline then reads through paragraphs with wide gaps and a deep middle band, crisp at small sizes.
